RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the November 19, 2007/Kartika 28, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Penalty in dowry death
cases
*41. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the reasons behind the Law
Commission's recommendation not to
prescribe capital punishment in dowry
death cases;
(b) whether the Commission's
recommendations are binding on
Government or are only persuasive in
nature; and
(c) what would be the legal position in
case the dowry death falls within the ambit
of offence of murder?
Policy for non-conventional energy
schemes
*42. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any non-conventional energy
policy in the country;
(b) if so, the details and the features
thereof and the role of such policy in rural,
tribal and remote areas of the country;
(c) whether this policy is being
implemented in the country;
(d) if so, the details of funds allocated,
released and actually spent on
implementation of various projects in rural
areas of the country during the last three
years, till date, project-wise, State-wise and
year-wise; and
(e) the details of non-conventional
energy sources which are operational at
present, alongwith the potential sources
for the same, State-wise?
Involvement of corporates for reforms
in higher education
*43. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether recently in the meeting
13

14
between the Prime Minister and the Union
Minister, a broad consensus has emerged
favouring involvement of corporates for
resource mobilization for reforms in higher
education;
(b) whether a campaign of Full Planning
Commission on Education for reforms in
institutions like UGC and AICTE took a
decisive shape in the month of September
and there was an overwhelming support
for adoption of Chinese models on the
expansion of higher education; and
(c) the steps being taken to improve
higher education in the country?
Loans to tribals in Jharkhand
*44. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are seized of
the fact that the Scheduled Tribes people in
Jharkhand are denied loans by Commercial
Banks and Financial Institutions beyond a
term exceeding five years, even where such
loans are secured by borrowers, by
mortgaging their land properties;
(b) if so, the reasons for depriving
Scheduled Tribes in Jharkhand of the
benefit of long term loans against security;
(c) whether Government are
contemplating steps to amend the situation;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Forest Rights Act
*45. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that even though
the Forest Rights Act was passed in 2006,
the rules have not been notified as yet; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Target for additional power
generation
†*46. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a target of
creating 10,159 Mega Watts power
generation capacity in the country for
2007-08 was fixed;
(b) if not, what was that target;
(c) whether it is also a fact that projects
related to creation of 2,645 MW power
generation capacity only were completed
from April to September, 2007; and
(d) if not, the facts in this regard?
Report on the development of
instrumentation
*47. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) the major recommendations of the
report prepared by the Indian National
Science Academy on development of
instrumentation in the country and
submitted to the Principal Scientific
Advisor; and

Withdrawal of Life Support System

member panel of reputed medical persons,
to clear the decision to withdraw Life
Support System from the terminally ill and
that patients and their relatives should
notify a High Court of the decision, so that
the doctor is immune from legal action;
(b) whether the Commission cited
several decisions of USA, Britain, Canada
and Australia and maintained that

RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for  WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the November 19, 2007/Kartika 28, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 79
Electronic measurement of
earthquakes
87. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any scheme to set up electronic
system for accurate measurement of
intensity of earthquakes, in the wake of
severe earthquake of October, 2005;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) by when this system is proposed to
be set up; and
(d) whether it would find out the
earthquakes from the atmospheric and
ocean current?
Instruments/computers for weather
forecasting
88. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the instruments/computers
available for weather forecasting, ocean
information and tropical meteorology are
completely out-dated;
(b) if so, whether Government are
planning to buy/produce super computers
for tracking changes in the climate of the
country;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the funds allocated for the purpose?
Shortage of food processing units in
Rajasthan
89. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of food processing units in
Rajasthan; and
(b) if so, the incentives Government
plan to give for setting up more such units
in that State?
Grants for food processing industries
in Sikkim
90. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of financial assistance
granted for setting up of food processing

24
industries in the country under various
schemes, particularly in Sikkim; and
(b) the details of amount spent on
setting up of food processing industries in
the country during the last three years,
State-wise?
Objectives of SSA
91. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the objectives of the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan;
(b) whether these objectives have been
achieved;
(c) if not, how much time has lapsed
between the target dates and today;
(d) the reasons for failure in
achievement of targets;
(e) what percentage of the child
population remains out of school on this
day;
(f) by when these children would be
brought under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
Programme;
(g) what steps are being taken to
accelerate the achievement of targets; and
(h) what percentage of funds is being
utilized to achieve these targets?
Setting up of new universities
92. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up 30
new universities for expanding access to
higher education in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
the universities that would be set up in
Orissa;
(c) whether it is also proposed to set up
6,000 quality schools, one in each block
of the country, to secure excellence in
public schooling; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, indicating
inter-alia, those that are proposed to be set
up in Orissa?
Education in the National Common
Minimum Programme
93. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:  Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of steps initiated by
Government  to fulfil the promises made
in the National Common Minimum
Programme in regard to education;
(b) whether the Right to Education,
enshrined in the Constitution, has been
fulfilled;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken to provide free and
compulsory education to children?
Expenditure on education
94. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) what is the percentage of GDP
towards higher education, primary and
middle education during the last three
years;
(b) how it compares with the developed
countries; and

25
(c) whether Government plan to
increase this in the coming years?
High illiteracy rate States
95. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:  Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether eight States alone account
for nearly 70 per cent of the country's
illiterates; which means that out of 304
million illiterate people in the country,
212.19 million come from these eight
States alone;
(b) whether, according to the recently
released reports on the status of adult
literacy in the country, 13 States need to
pay special attention for raising their
literacy levels;
(c) if so, whether this report was
brought out by the National Literacy
Mission; and
